questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of end-to-end data governance in a CNPA stack and the practical application of the outbox pattern for atomicity and auditability.

## Key Concepts

- Transactional outbox pattern
- Append-only audit store
- Payload hashing for integrity
- End-to-end provenance across HTTP, DB, Kafka
- Idempotent Kafka publishers and exactly-once semantics

## Code Example

```javascript
// pseudo: upsert user and audit row in one transaction
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES ($1, $2)
  ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name;
INSERT INTO audit_outbox (id, user_id, action, ts, payload_hash, source)
  VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $3, now(), hashof($4), 'HTTP');
COMMIT;
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle auditing latency vs. throughput?
- How would you test disaster recovery of the audit trail?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question assesses advanced triage capabilities for end-to-end CNPA (Containerized N-tier Platform Architecture) flows under backpressure conditions in a data lake pipeline. It evaluates understanding of distributed systems resilience, observability across heterogeneous components, and practical performance optimization techniques.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end distributed tracing across HTTP, database, Kafka, Redis, and data sink
- Backpressure propagation mechanics and mitigation strategies (circuit breakers, bounded queues)
- Exactly-once vs. at-least-once delivery semantics
- Kafka producer configuration for durability and throughput
- Redis caching strategies and TTL management
- Observability best practices with OpenTelemetry
